input: Learn to whistle with fingers in my mouth

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to learn how to produce a whistle sound using their fingers placed inside their mouth.

questions.title: Which finger configuration are you aiming for?
questions.description: Identify the specific finger placement style the user wants to learn, such as two index fingers, two pinkies, or one hand using index and middle finger.

questions.title: Have you ever produced any sound attempting this?
questions.description: Understand the user's current baseline — whether they are a complete beginner or have gotten close to making a sound before.

questions.title: What is your main reason for learning this skill?
questions.description: Clarify the motivation behind learning finger whistling, such as hailing a cab, signaling at events, or impressing others.

questions.title: How much daily practice time can you realistically commit?
questions.description: Determine how many minutes per day the user can dedicate to practice so the plan can be paced accordingly.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline or target date in mind?
questions.description: Find out if the user needs to learn this skill by a specific date or event, which affects the urgency and intensity of the plan.

questions.title: Do you prefer learning from written steps or videos?
questions.description: Understand the user's preferred learning format so resources and instructions can be recommended accordingly.

questions.title: Are there any physical constraints with your fingers or mouth?
questions.description: Check for any relevant physical limitations such as dental work, braces, or finger injuries that might affect technique or approach.
